reviewBoundary: Three complete senior original clozes. Fictional knitting, chess and anonymous-judging narratives. Same-author all-key and alternative review, shuffled options; no independent calibration claimed.

units.title: The scarf with one wide end

materials.title: The scarf with one wide end
materials.text:
I decided to knit a scarf for my uncle. He cycled to work even in winter, and I wanted to give him something ____1____. Grandma taught me the first few rows, then let me continue.

At first, the scarf grew straight. Later, I began to lose count. One end became much ____2____ than the other. I put it in a drawer and considered buying a gift instead.

Grandma asked to see it. I expected her to tell me to ____3____, but she showed me how to keep the remaining rows even. "You can learn from this one without making it disappear," she said.

I finished the scarf and washed it as she instructed. It was soft, though hardly ____4____. On my uncle's birthday, I explained the wide end before he opened the parcel. He wrapped it around his neck and went to look in the ____5____.

"This end covers the gap in my coat," he said. I thought he was being ____6____. Then, a week later, I saw him leave for work wearing it.

He did not claim it was the best scarf ever made. He said it was warm, and that he liked knowing who had ____7____ it. Both reasons mattered.

I asked Grandma to help me begin another. This time, I counted more ____8____ and checked each row. Accepting the first scarf did not mean refusing to ____9____.

When my uncle visited, he showed me a loose thread. I felt a sudden wave of ____10____, but he simply asked whether we could mend it. The scarf was not an exhibit that had to remain untouched. It was being ____11____.

We fixed the thread together. I began to enjoy the idea that a gift could have a life ____12____ the moment it was opened. Its uneven shape was still there, but it no longer ____13____ everything else. I had made something imperfect and useful. That was enough to keep me ____14____, with a little more skill and much less ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Winter cycling motivates a warm scarf. Cost, weight and formality do not address the stated cold-weather need.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The title and later gap coverage identify one wide end. Shorter concerns length, darker colour and older age, not the uneven width.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The narrator expects beginning again, contrasted with continuing and retaining this scarf. Advertising and celebrating do not address the error; hiding has already happened and is not the teacher’s correction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The scarf is soft but visibly uneven, so hardly perfect. Soft/warm are its benefits, and washing does not establish it remains wet.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: He checks how the wrapped scarf looks in a mirror. Drawer, road and the already opened parcel are not reflective surfaces.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The narrator suspects tactful politeness rather than genuine approval. Carelessness and anger do not fit his positive comment; he is speaking, not silent.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The niece/nephew knitted it, so the uncle knows who made it. Sale, borrowing and loss are not its origin.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: More careful counting addresses lost stitches/counts. Speed, silence and secrecy do not prevent counting errors.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Keeping the first imperfect attempt is compatible with improving the next. The narrator did finish and share it; rest is not the skill question.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: A loose thread initially disappoints the maker. Hunger and sleepiness are physical states, while excitement is not the immediate worry.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Regular wear and a repair show use, contrasted with an untouched exhibit. Hiding, mere display and replacement do not explain wear.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: A gift’s life extends beyond opening into use and repair. Before reverses the timeline; against/within do not express continuation afterwards.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The uneven shape no longer defines the gift’s entire value. It does not itself warm, cover or repair everything else.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The narrator continues learning to knit. Cycling is the uncle’s activity, shopping the abandoned alternative and waiting not the skill.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Acceptance and learning reduce fear of imperfection. The narrator still needs wool, time and practice rather than reducing those as the lesson.

units.title: The chair on the other side
units.alignmentNote: One complete original fifteen-gap four-choice narrative, National I final structure. Old source is a level/family drafting reference only.

materials.title: The chair on the other side
materials.text:
Our chess coach asked us to change places halfway through a practice game. I was pleased with my position and thought the suggestion ____1____. Why should I give away the advantage I had built?

The result would not count towards our league. The exercise was to examine a position from both ____2____. Reluctantly, I moved to my opponent's chair.

My first glance was uncomfortable. From here, the attack I had admired looked less ____3____. There was a gap beside my former king that I had barely noticed. My opponent smiled.

I wanted to prove my earlier plan was still good. That made my first move from the new chair ____4____. I defended against the move I expected instead of considering the choices now available to me.

The coach asked what I would advise a beginner sitting in my place. The question created a little ____5____ from my pride. I looked again and found a simple defensive move.

We continued for another fifteen minutes, then discussed the game without declaring a ____6____. My original position had strengths, but it had not been as safe as I assumed. The same was true of my opponent's.

Changing chairs had not supplied a magic ____7____. It had made a familiar board unfamiliar enough for me to ____8____ it again. I realised how easily I confused a plan I had made with a plan that must be ____9____.

At our next ordinary match, I stayed in my own chair.  But before choosing a move, I tried to imagine the reply from the other ____10____. Sometimes that confirmed my plan; sometimes it exposed a ____11____. 

I still wanted to win. Learning another viewpoint had not removed ____12____. It had made my ambition less dependent on defending every earlier decision. A good move could require ____13____ a favourite idea. When the coach next asked us to swap, I went willingly. The other chair no longer meant my work was ____14____. It was a place from which I might finally see what I had ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Giving up a built advantage initially seems unfair to the narrator. Helpful is the later view; generous and ordinary do not match the protest.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Changing opponents’ seats examines both sides of one board. Years, rooms and leagues do not name those opposed viewpoints.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The visible weakness makes the formerly admired attack less convincing. Price, familiarity and colour do not express its reduced strategic credibility.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Ignoring the actual options leads to a poor move. No rule violation, brilliant result or popular approval is established.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Advising an imagined beginner creates distance from pride and allows reassessment. Anger and noise are absent; delay alone does not express detachment.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: They discuss the non-league exercise without declaring a winner. Rule, date and venue are not the result normally announced.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The swap does not give an automatic solution; it enables fresh examination. Board/opponent already existed and no prize is at issue.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Seeing it freshly permits examination. Ignoring, decorating and selling do not evaluate the position.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The error is assuming authorship makes a plan correct. Mine merely restates ownership, and early/popular do not establish strategic truth.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The imagined reply comes from the other side of the board. Room/league/teacher do not identify the opponent’s position.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Reconsideration can expose a weakness in the plan. Prize, secret and colour are not the strategic problem contrasted with confirmation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The narrator still wants to win, so ambition remains. Patience and friendship are not the desire described, and rules have already stayed in force.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: A better move may require abandoning a favourite idea. Repeating/hiding do not change it; publishing is unrelated to a game decision.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The initial fear was losing the value of work already done. The new view rejects that it is wasted. Praise/display/protection do not express the feared loss.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The other perspective reveals what was missed. Created, saved and promised do not name overlooked strategic details.

materials.title: Before the names were revealed
materials.text:
Having won our village show’s student photography section years earlier, I expected judging it to be ____1____. Then the organiser handed me twelve prints with no names attached.

I recognised one garden immediately. Known for spectacular flowers, it seemed certain to earn a high ____2____. But the image itself was awkward: a bright bin occupied one corner, and the main flower was lost against the background.

Another picture showed an ordinary weed beside a cracked wall. Its subject seemed ____3____. Looking longer, I noticed how the small leaves caught the light. The photographer had made a neglected corner worth ____4____.

The organiser asked us to use the stated criteria: composition, clarity of intention and effective use of light. We could not award points for the ____5____ of the garden or the effort we imagined behind the picture.

I put the familiar image aside, reread the criteria and returned to it. That did not improve the photograph; it exposed how much my first impression relied on ____6____ rather than the submitted work.

We disagreed, but the criteria made our discussion more ____7____. We could explain what each photograph achieved instead of simply defending a favourite.

The weed picture won. Its maker was a new student none of us knew. My pleasure contained a little ____8____: familiarity had almost guided me elsewhere.

Anonymous judging had not made us perfectly ____9____. We still brought different tastes and experiences. It had, however, removed one easy ____10____ for a quick decision. The criteria gave us another reason to slow down.

I asked the winner where she had found the spot. She pointed behind the hall. I had walked past it for years. Her photograph had ____11____ my attention. Judging it fairly required a similar movement, from what I already ____12____ to what was actually there. I returned the prints more ____13____ about my own first reactions, and more willing to let an unfamiliar image ____14____ its place. The award belonged to a photograph, not a ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Previous success makes the narrator expect an easy or straightforward task. Pointlessness, impossibility and danger do not follow from that confidence.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: A judged photograph receives a score. Price is commercial, shelf/fence physical structures, not evaluation points.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: An ordinary weed seems unremarkable before close viewing. Fame and expense oppose the ordinary status; nothing suggests unreality.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The image directs attention to a neglected corner, making it worth noticing. Removing, selling and watering are not effects of photographic composition on the viewer.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The narrator’s initial bias comes from a well-known garden’s reputation. Size/colour/location are physical features, not the external status excluded by image criteria.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Recognising a prestigious garden affects the initial assessment. Light, clarity and composition are legitimate image criteria rather than the external familiarity being exposed.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Criteria allow precise explanations of what images achieve. Personal merely intensifies subjective preference; permanence and popularity do not describe evidence-based discussion.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The narrator feels relief that familiarity did not determine the winner. Boredom, complete certainty and anger are not supported by the pleased retrospective concern.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Different tastes mean anonymity does not guarantee perfect objectivity. Silence, fame and invisibility are not measures of fair assessment.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Familiar status offers an easy shortcut to a quick decision. Reward is an outcome, question/argument require thinking rather than substituting for it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The photograph redirects attention to an overlooked place. Division, measurement and exhaustion do not express that new focus.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The fair movement is from prior assumptions to the actual work. The narrator had not photographed/awarded this image, and forgotten does not name the initial bias.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Recognising a near-bias makes the narrator cautious about first reactions. Certainty/carelessness reverse it; excitement is not the self-evaluative change.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: An unfamiliar image should earn its place through its merits. Borrow, hide and exchange do not express deserved recognition.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The submitted photograph is judged on its merits, not the fame of the garden it depicts. Camera, frame and judge’s chair are equipment rather than the familiar subject’s status.
